key_insight: An AI-agent-assisted, Lean-verified pipeline checks whether a quantum device’s effective Hamiltonian preserves the intended topological code’s low-energy subspace.
engineering_relevance: The workflow identifies viable device parameters and dominant unwanted interactions to guide coupling and control improvements for analog quantum error correction.
method: Construct the ideal code Hamiltonian and determine its protective excitation gap.
Check low-energy state isolation and subspace agreement using Lean.
Compare unwanted energy-shift bounds from interaction-strength sums, anticommuting Pauli grouping, and diagonalization.
evidence_signal: For an eight-qubit toric-code model on a superconducting device, the agent found parameters within a prescribed leakage budget, and Lean verified four isolated low-energy states close to the ideal code space.
watch_item: The guarantees concern an effective device model; robustness to experimental noise, model mismatch, and larger arrays remains to be established.
paper_title: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware
